findings.finding: Provider completion could outlive cancellation/deadline or invoke provider factory before preflight.
findings.resolution: Preflight, post-poll and post-parse cancellation/deadline checks; factory-no-call and delayed-ready regression tests pass.

findings.finding: Equivalent regenerated previews shared consent digest; failed topology application could retain newly issued execution authority.
findings.resolution: Fresh random proposal identity/lifetime/action/input/plan/UI/policy digest binding; single-use stored proposal; failure revokes only newly issued execution consent; replay/quota tests pass.

findings.finding: Revocation/cancellation during discovery or final validation could still dispatch inference or publish preview.
findings.resolution: Private Session owns Kernel/Rooms; per-room token-identity lease, pre-dispatch/post-validation fences, retained cancellation token and monotonic policy epoch; concurrent room tests pass.

findings.finding: Audit omitted early failures, correlation, native errors and partial initialization stages.
findings.resolution: Bounded prompt-free audit records unique host correlations, revision, pin, status, native/public codes and topology/initialization stages; privacy and partial-failure tests pass.

findings.finding: Queued preparation ownership depended on caller-controlled cross-channel token equality.
findings.resolution: Cleanup compares host Cancellation identity and only rejected Operator Prepare requests; adversarial queue ownership tests pass.

findings.finding: Large audit replies could terminate transport or erase committed outcome on overflow.
findings.resolution: Audit tail limited to16, metadata caps, bounded serialization strips audit first and retains authoritative stage fields in final fallback; overflow regression passes.

findings.finding: Failed initial topology persistence incorrectly offered installed-form recovery; approval cancellation/watchdog could hide committed results.
findings.resolution: Separate topologyCheckpointPersisted field and stage-aware native/Qt recovery; approval is documented commit boundary, Cancel disabled after confirmation, watchdog preserves authoritative reply; actual filesystem/trap and genuine Qt repair tests pass.

findings.finding: Intent edits could leave reusable UI consent and raw Proposal application was externally callable.
findings.resolution: Intent edits clear displayed consent; trusted preview uses plain text and explicit unchecked confirmation; raw Proposal/ApplyContext are crate-private and only owned Session applies; genuine consent tests pass.

findings.finding: Supplemental length constraints and public error taxonomy differed from ADR005.
findings.resolution: UTF-8 byte limits,512-scalar explanation limits, strict duplicate/unknown-field parsing and ADR error wrapping now enforced and adversarial corpus/boundary tests pass.

limitations: No external model adapter, auto-approval, privileged component, multi-component or general natural-language inference approval.
Provider deadline is cooperative for trusted native adapters; arbitrary blocking native code is not isolated by this interface.
Checkpoint callbacks are trusted bounded persistence I/O and must not re-enter Session; this precondition is documented and actual worker callback complies.
Cancellation/revocation after approved apply begins serializes after that commit boundary; no interruption claim.
Separate runtime review, full retained regressions, successful hosted Linux run and downloaded archive verification remain milestone acceptance gates. ADR005 remains PROPOSED.
